per_item.user_input: What is the difference between a COR and a COG?
per_item.response: A COR (Certificate of Registration) is a document issued to a licensed professional, confirming their registration and licensure to practice. A COG (Certificate of Good Standing) certifies that a professional is in good standing with their licensing body, indicating they have no pending violations or disciplinary actions.
per_item.reference: The COR (Certificate of Registration) certifies that you are officially enrolled for the semester; it is required for admission to classes and for processing a student ID, and can be viewed on the portal or claimed as a printed copy at the Registrar. The COG (Copy of Grades) is the official record of your grades for a semester issued by the Registrar; its information is also shown on the LSPU Portal.

Article 3. Minor Offense

Sec. 1. Attendance

1.1. Attending flag raising and flag lowering ceremonies (R.A. 8491 Sec. 18 and 50 Philippine Flag Law), classes, and other required University activities regularly and on time is required for all students unless exemption is granted by the University President or his duly authorized representative.

1.2 Tardiness and absences shall be dealt with as follows:

1.2.1 Tardiness in all activities where student’s attendance is required shall be considered one (1) absence in class.

1.2.2 Three (3) tardiness in a class shall be considered one (1) absence from the same.
 1st Offense: One (1) day absent plus community service
 2nd Offense: Inform the parents/guardians with three (3) days suspension
 3rd Offense: Suspension for one (1) week

1.2.3. Every student accumulating unexcused absences from class equivalent to 17% of the total number of hours/ semester for a particular subject or class shall be dropped from the roll of students. However, excused absences can be removed through makeup.

1.2.4. Every student shall secure an excuse slip from the Guidance Office for absence/s made before admission to classes.

Source: reporting to the College Dean is from campus information supplied by the maintainer (September 2026). The written complaint to OSAS and the committee are from the Student Handbook, Chapter 6, Articles 2 and 6 (Anti-Bullying Act of 2013, RA 10627, is the legal basis of the bullying offenses). Steps 1 and 4 are practical advice.
Bullying or harassment must be reported to your College Dean so it is noted and can be solved quickly. Four steps:
Step 1: Write down what happened. Note who was involved, what happened, when and where, and who saw it. For online bullying, keep screenshots and links. Do this while the details are fresh; it makes the report faster to act on.
Step 2: Tell your College Dean. Report it as soon as possible. The Dean notes the case and acts on it quickly at the college level; the Dean is also a member of the Student Discipline Committee for students of that college.
Step 3: File a signed written complaint with OSAS when formal action is needed. OSAS handles all complaints against alleged violators of the Code of Conduct.

Article 1. Rights of Students (Lifted from: Art. II. The Educational Community, Chapter 2. Rights, Section 9)

In addition to other rights under existing laws, and subject to limitations prescribed by law and regulations, students shall enjoy the following rights:

a. The right to receive, primarily through competent instruction, relevant quality education in line with national goals and conducive to their full development as person with human dignity.

b. The right to freely choose their field of study subject to the existing curricula and to continue their course therein up to graduation, except in cases of academic deficiency, or violation of disciplinary regulations

c. The right to guidance and counseling services for making decisions and selecting the alternatives in fields of work suited to their potentialities.

d. The right to access to their own academic records, the confidentiality of which the university shall maintain and preserve.

2.1.2. midterm examination: 25% of balance

2.1.3. final examination: the remaining balance

per_item.response:
The steps to request a Transcript of Records are:

1. For new students/transferees:
   - Secure the Enrolment Slip from the Admission Office.
   - Obtain the Original Certificate of Good Moral Character from the previous school.
   - Get the Original Report Card from the PSA office.
   - Provide a photocopy of PSA Birth Certificate or Marriage Contract for married female students.
   - Submit the Original/authenticated Form 137 (for new students).
   - Acquire a Medical slip/Certificate from LSPU Medical Clinic.
   - Request the Transcript of Records/Copy of Grades from the previous school for client evaluation purposes.
   - Provide 2 pieces of 2x2 pictures.
   - Submit the Original Certificate of Transfer (for transferees).
   - Prepare 1 long brown envelope.

2. For old students:
   - Secure a Clearance from the school previously attended/graduated.
   - Submit a Student ID.
   - Provide an Evaluation of Grades from the Registrar/College.
   - Provide 2 pieces of 2x2 pictures.
   - Submit the Original Certificate of Transfer (for transferees).
   - Prepare 1 long brown envelope.

3. The client (student) proceeds to the Registrar:
   - The Registrar validates the authenticity of the submitted documents (8 minutes).
   - The Registrar enlists subjects to the system and issues SF10/F137 request forms.
   - The Registrar checks if grades or grades changes are needed (5 minutes).

4. Payment:
   - The client pays P30.00 per unit.

5. The Registrar processes the request:
   - Confirm/approve the subjects to be credited (5 minutes).

6. The Registrar completes the processing, and the Transcript of Records is prepared for release.
per_item.reference: Step 1: fill out the request slip (LSPU-REG-SF-011) with clearance and signatures of the heads of responsible offices; graduates fill out the same slip. Step 2: pay the required fees at the Cashier's Office (TOR is P75.00 per page for undergraduate and P150.00 per page for graduate). Step 3: submit the request slip and official receipt and receive a claim stub with the release date while the Registrar prepares the document. Step 4: claim the document on the date on the claim stub. Total service time is up to 59 minutes for active files and 1 day plus about 44 minutes for inactive files.

The application uses the prescribed form stating the reasons, with a copy of grades certified by the registrar. A request submitted or received later is not considered for the following semester.

To apply online for the completion of an INC grade at LSPU-LB campus, follow these steps:

1. Log in to your portal in the LSPU online system after submitting the complete requirements to your subject teacher.
2. Pay the corresponding completion fee of P30.00 to the cashier’s office, who will then put the OR P30.00 number on your completion form through the online system (this process takes about 5 minutes).
3. Inform your subject teacher that you have applied for online completion of your INC/4.0 grade; the teacher will then give the corresponding grades through the online system (this step takes about 5 minutes).
4. The college dean or associate dean will check and approve the request for completion/removal (this step takes about 5 minutes).
5. The registrar will verify if the INC or 4.0 grade has been changed (this step takes about 5 minutes).

Total process time is approximately 25 minutes.

Total processing time is 25 minutes.

The difference between a COR (Certificate of Registration) and a COG (Copy of Grades) is as follows:

- A COR (Certificate of Registration) is issued to students to confirm their enrollment status and registration for a semester. It is obtained by students who proceed to the Cashier's Office to pay fees or log into the student portal to view their registration certificate. It reflects the student's current registration status for a specific term.

- A COG (Copy of Grades) is issued at the end of a semester by the Office of the Registrar. It indicates the student's grades for the courses/subjects taken during that semester and includes any concerns about the student's standing, such as INC, warning, probation, dismissal, or disqualification. It is used for monitoring and assessing the student's academic performance and standing.
per_item.reference: The COR (Certificate of Registration) certifies that you are officially enrolled for the semester; it is required for admission to classes and for processing a student ID, and can be viewed on the portal or claimed as a printed copy at the Registrar. The COG (Copy of Grades) is the official record of your grades for a semester issued by the Registrar; its information is also shown on the LSPU Portal.

Article 3. Minor Offense

Sec. 1. Attendance

1.1. Attending flag raising and flag lowering ceremonies (R.A. 8491 Sec. 18 and 50 Philippine Flag Law), classes, and other required University activities regularly and on time is required for all students unless exemption is granted by the University President or his duly authorized representative.

1.2 Tardiness and absences shall be dealt with as follows:

1.2.1 Tardiness in all activities where student’s attendance is required shall be considered one (1) absence in class.

1.2.2 Three (3) tardiness in a class shall be considered one (1) absence from the same.
 1st Offense: One (1) day absent plus community service

1.2.3. Every student accumulating unexcused absences from class equivalent to 17% of the total number of hours/ semester for a particular subject or class shall be dropped from the roll of students. However, excused absences can be removed through makeup.

1.2.4. Every student shall secure an excuse slip from the Guidance Office for absence/s made before admission to classes.

Sec. 2. Dishonesty.

Article 8. Attendance

Sec. 1. Policy. A student absent from classes for unavoidable cause must obtain an excuse slip from the Office of the Students Affairs Services or Guidance Office. The slip must be presented to the instructor/ professor concerned not later than the second class session, following the student’s return with a medical certification for absence due to illness.

Sec. 2. Absence. A student accumulating unexcused absences from class, equivalent to twenty percent (25%) of the total number of hours per day session for a particular subject, shall be dropped from the roll of students for the particular subject or class, as the case may be. Time lost due to late enrolment shall be considered as a time lost by absence.

Source: reporting to the College Dean is from campus information supplied by the maintainer (September 2026). The written complaint to OSAS and the committee are from the Student Handbook, Chapter 6, Articles 2 and 6 (Anti-Bullying Act of 2013, RA 10627, is the legal basis of the bullying offenses). Steps 1 and 4 are practical advice.
Bullying or harassment must be reported to your College Dean so it is noted and can be solved quickly. Four steps:
Step 1: Write down what happened. Note who was involved, what happened, when and where, and who saw it. For online bullying, keep screenshots and links. Do this while the details are fresh; it makes the report faster to act on.
Step 2: Tell your College Dean. Report it as soon as possible. The Dean notes the case and acts on it quickly at the college level; the Dean is also a member of the Student Discipline Committee for students of that college.
Step 3: File a signed written complaint with OSAS when formal action is needed. OSAS handles all complaints against alleged violators of the Code of Conduct.

per_item.response:
The steps to request a Transcript of Records are as follows:

1. Pay the required fees at the Cashier’s Office:
   - Undergrad students: P75.00 per page
   - Graduate students: P150.00 per page
   - Certifications: P30.00 per page
2. Fill out the request slip (LSPU-REG-SF-011).
3. Review and check the accomplished request slip, and assess the corresponding fees of requested documents.
4. Secure signatures of responsible offices.
5. Proceed to the Cashier’s Office to pay the fees and receive an official receipt.
6. Submit the request slip and official receipt to the Registrar’s Office.
7. The Registrar’s Office will review and check the request, then process it.
8. The Records Management Office will receive and upload the approved request.
9. The approved request will be released after approximately 10 minutes.

Note: The evidence does not specify additional steps beyond payment, request slip completion, and processing, but these are the key steps identified.
per_item.reference: Step 1: fill out the request slip (LSPU-REG-SF-011) with clearance and signatures of the heads of responsible offices; graduates fill out the same slip. Step 2: pay the required fees at the Cashier's Office (TOR is P75.00 per page for undergraduate and P150.00 per page for graduate). Step 3: submit the request slip and official receipt and receive a claim stub with the release date while the Registrar prepares the document. Step 4: claim the document on the date on the claim stub. Total service time is up to 59 minutes for active files and 1 day plus about 44 minutes for inactive files.

Source: announcement channels from the maintainer (September 2026); safety steps are general disaster-safety guidance, NOT an LSPU-LB protocol. Who decides suspensions and the campus's own typhoon procedure were not supplied here (see the Student Handbook rules on suspension of classes).
Before: check the official LSPU-LB Facebook page for campus-wide class suspensions, and your professor's Messenger group and Google Classroom for class-level announcements, before you travel. Keep your phone charged.

SAFETY GUIDE: WHAT TO DO IN AN EARTHQUAKE
Source: general earthquake-safety guidance, NOT an LSPU-LB protocol. The campus's official evacuation areas and drill procedure were not supplied, so none are stated. Ask the Safety and Security Management Office.
During shaking: DROP to your hands and knees, take COVER under a sturdy desk or table (or protect your head and neck with your arms next to an inside wall), and HOLD ON until the shaking stops.
Stay away from windows, glass, shelves and heavy objects. If outdoors, move away from buildings, posts and wires. Do not run out during the shaking.
After it stops: leave the building calmly by the stairs (not the elevator) to an open area, expect aftershocks, and follow the guards and faculty.
Help others only if it is safe, and report injuries to a guard or the campus clinic. Call 911 for serious injuries or fire.

Sec. 5. INC Mark

5.1. Types of INC or Incomplete mark

5.1.1. No Final Examination. A grade of INC is given if a student whose class standing throughout the term/semester is passing but fails to take the final examination due to illness or other valid reason/s. An approved excuse slip is required before a student is given the examination. In case the student's class standing is not passing, and s/he fails the final examination for any reason, a grade of “5.0” is given. Re-examination to improve a passing grade is not allowed.

5.1.2. Failure to comply with certain requirements. INC is also given to the work that is of passing quality, but some parts of which are undone because of sickness or failure to comply with certain requirements of the course.

5.2. Policies for INC

5.2.1. A grade of INC is not given to any student with a failing grade in a subject. The one-year academic period is interrupted as extending to the regular semester; the removal period immediately follows the one year.

1.3. Host Training Establishment (HTE) refers to agencies, institutions, or establishments whom the University has partnered with and entrusted the students for work immersion and learning experience.

1.4. Internship Manual refers to the document detailing the policies and guidelines for the conduct of the internship/on-the-job training of the students.

1.5. Internship Plan refers to the curriculum and competency outline detailing what the student should be able to attain in the course of the internship/on-the-job training program as prepared and approved by the University and the HTE.

1.6. Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) refers to the document that records the details of an agreement between the University and the HTE, detailing the objectives, plan, scope, expectations and activities among other composites of the agreement.

A COG (Copy of Grades) is issued at the end of the semester by the Office of the Registrar, indicating the grades for courses taken and any concerns about the student's standing, such as INC, warning, probation, dismissal, or disqualification.
per_item.reference: The COR (Certificate of Registration) certifies that you are officially enrolled for the semester; it is required for admission to classes and for processing a student ID, and can be viewed on the portal or claimed as a printed copy at the Registrar. The COG (Copy of Grades) is the official record of your grades for a semester issued by the Registrar; its information is also shown on the LSPU Portal.

SECTION: Chapter 3 | Article 7. Grading System and Other Grade-related Concerns
of GWA

4.1. GWA. The General Weighted Average or GWA of students refers to the weighted average of grades in all academic courses taken in a given semester.

4.2. Cumulative GWA. Cumulative GWA is the weighted average of the grades in all academic courses from the first semester in which the student was enrolled up to the second semester just finished.

Sec. 5. Policy on Grades of “4” and “5”

5.1. Appearance of “4”. To compute the General Weighted Average

(GWA) of a student with a grade of “4”, use the latter as an actual grade on the premise that “4” is conditional.

5.2. Appearance of “5”. If the student gets a removal grade of “5”, this grade is included in the computation of the GWA together with the grade which s/he gets after re-enrolling and passing the course.

The GWA should be the basis for determining if the student graduates with or without honors.

5.3. Removal Policy for “4.00”. A grade of “4.00” may be removed by repeating the subject or by re-examination. The highest grade a student must obtain upon re-examination is “3.00”. If the removal examination is failed, a student is given a grade of “5.00”.

per_item.response:
The steps to request a Transcript of Records are as follows:

1. Fill out and endorse the request slip (LSPU-REG-SF-011), which involves:
   - Issues the request slip
   - Reviews and checks the accomplished request against the student's clearance
   - Assesses the corresponding fees of the requested documents
   - Undergraduates fill out the request slip with clearance and secure signatures of heads of responsible offices; graduates fill out the same request slip
   - Time required: 5 minutes

2. Pay the required fees at the Cashier's Office, which involves:
   - Receiving payment and issuing an official receipt
   - Fees vary depending on the document:
     - Transcript of Records: P75.00/page (undergraduate), P150.00/page (graduate)
     - Certifications: P30.00/page
     - Authentication: P30.00/page
     - 2nd copy of Diploma: P100.00
   - Time required: 2 minutes

3. Submit the receipt and request slip, receive the claim stub, and document preparation, which involves:
   - Receiving and reviewing the presented receipt and request slip
   - Scheduling the date of release
   - Issuing claim stub
   - Locating the permanent record
   - Preparing and encoding the requested document
   - Reviewing and counterchecking entries
   - Printing the final document
   - Affixing the college seal
   - Signing the document
   - Time required: up to 59 minutes total (including locating record, preparing/encoding, review, printing, sealing, signing)

4. Claim the requested document on the scheduled date indicated on the claim stub, which involves:
   - Claiming the document
   - Time required: 2 minutes
per_item.reference: Step 1: fill out the request slip (LSPU-REG-SF-011) with clearance and signatures of the heads of responsible offices; graduates fill out the same slip. Step 2: pay the required fees at the Cashier's Office (TOR is P75.00 per page for undergraduate and P150.00 per page for graduate). Step 3: submit the request slip and official receipt and receive a claim stub with the release date while the Registrar prepares the document. Step 4: claim the document on the date on the claim stub. Total service time is up to 59 minutes for active files and 1 day plus about 44 minutes for inactive files.

On the LSPU Portal, you can do the following:

1. Enlist subjects for enrollment
2. Check your enrollment status
3. Apply online for completion of INC or 4.0 grade
4. Request the school Google account
5. Verify grades against the Registrar's report
6. View your Certificate of Registration (COR)
7. View your grades
per_item.reference: On the LSPU Portal students can view their grades, check their enrollment status and academic standing flags (such as Warning, Probation and INC), enlist subjects for enrollment (old students), view the Certificate of Registration (COR), apply online for completion of an INC or 4.0 grade, verify printed grades against the Registrar's report, and request the school Google account.

h:additionalInfo: 15 of the 23 programs lead to a PRC licensure examination: BS Psychology (Psychometrician), BS Accountancy (CPA), BS Criminology (Criminologist), BS Fisheries (Fisheries Professional Licensure Examination, formerly the Fisheries Technologist exam), BS Food Technology (Food Technologists Licensure Examination), BS Nutrition and Dietetics (Nutritionist-Dietitian), and all 9 CTE teacher-education programs (Licensure Examination for Teachers: Elementary for BEEd, Secondary for the rest). The 8 programs without a board exam are BS Computer Science, both BS Business Administration majors, the three BS Information Technology majors, BS Tourism Management, and BS Hospitality Management.
h:additionalInfo: All 23 LSPU-LB programs. CAS: BS Psychology. CBAA: BS Accountancy; BS Business Administration major in Marketing Management; BS Business Administration major in Financial Management. CCS: BS Computer Science major in Intelligent Systems; BS Information Technology majors in Animation and Motion Graphics, Web and Mobile Application Development, and Service Management Program. CCJE: BS Criminology. CF: BS Fisheries. CFND: BS Food Technology; BS Nutrition and Dietetics. CIHT: BS Tourism Management; BS Hospitality Management. CTE: BS Education majors in English, Filipino, Mathematics, Sciences, and Social Studies; Bachelor of Elementary Education; Bachelor of Technology and Livelihood Education major in Home Economics; Bachelor of Technical-Vocational Teacher Education major in Food and Service Management; Bachelor of Physical Education.
h:additionalInfo: Campus-wide: the Supreme Student Council (SSC), the main student government. Named organizations: Legion of Lures Esports (LURES), Psychology Society (College of Arts and Sciences), Ka-Peer Yu Organization (peer support, working with the Guidance and Counseling Unit), EsKultura (cultural and arts, with Himig EsKultura and Likha EsKultura), Ritmo EsKultura (official dance club), and Bay Breeze Group of Publications (campus publication). Each of the 8 colleges also has its own student council, including the CCS Student Council (CCS-SC), and the colleges have their own student organizations. Full membership lists were not supplied.
h:additionalInfo: For a life-threatening emergency call 911 (national hotline) and tell the nearest guard. On campus: the Guard House at the main gate (left as you enter) for any security concern; the University Health Service clinic for medical help; the Guidance Office for emotional crisis; and your College Dean for bullying or harassment. The campus main line is (049) 308-4530 (Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM), but it is not an emergency line and it is not answered after office hours; for emergencies use 911 or a guard.
h:additionalInfo: LSPU-LB offers 23 degree programs across 8 colleges. All 23 are 4-year bachelor's programs. By college: College of Teacher Education (CTE) 9; College of Computer Studies (CCS) 4; College of Business Administration and Accountancy (CBAA) 3; College of Food Nutrition and Dietetics (CFND) 2; College of Hospitality Management and Tourism (CIHT) 2; College of Arts and Sciences (CAS) 1; College of Criminal Justice Education (CCJE) 1; College of Fisheries (CF) 1. Of the 23, 15 lead to a PRC licensure examination and 8 do not.
h:additionalInfo: Main events: (1) ICAC-CAF, the sports and cultural competition among colleges; the 2026 campus level was held September 15-18, 2026 and the university-wide ICAC-CAF is scheduled for October 20-23, 2026 at the LSPU Santa Cruz Campus. (2) The LSPU Founding Anniversary; the 73rd was celebrated with activities around November 26-28, 2025. (3) College weeks: each college has its own festival week during the year, such as CCS Week and CTE Week. Also, LURES took part in the 2026 February Fair esports competition.
h:additionalInfo: Office of the Registrar: enrollment, COR, TOR, transfer credentials, grades. Accounting Office: fee assessment and clearance. Cashier: payments. OSAS: student organizations, ID validation, clearances, good moral certificates, excuse slips. Guidance Office: entrance exam and counseling. Scholarship and Financial Assistance Unit: scholarships. University Health Service: medical and dental care. Business Affairs, Marketing and Production Office: Student ID, and the sale of the ID lace, uniform fabric, University shirt, NSTP shirt and PE uniform. ICT office (inside the CCS building): activation of the student portal account. Library: reference, circulation, facilities.
h:additionalInfo: The LSPU-LB campus is in Malinta, Los Baños, Laguna. Directions start at the main gate. Turn left for the Administration Building (Registrar and Cashier/Accounting on the 2nd floor), Joey Lina Gym, CHMT and COF, and CFND beside the Guard House. Walk straight in for the Clinic, Cafeteria, Business Affairs Office and Scholarship and Financial Assistance office. Turn right for the Hall, Gender and Development, CBAA, OSAS, the University President's office, CAS, Lacson Gym, CCS, CTE and the Alumni Building. CCJE is along the road to the right, and the Library is at the end of the road to the left, outside the gate. Places listed: Campus Main Gate and Entrance, Guard House, the Hall, CCS Building (College of Computer Studies), CAS Building (College of Arts and Sciences), CTE Building (College of Teacher Education), CBAA Building (College of Business Administration and Accountancy), CFND Faculty (College of Food Nutrition and Dietetics), CHMT Building (College of Hospitality Management and Tourism), COF Building (College of Fisheries), CCJE Building (College of Criminal Justice Education), Cafeteria, Lacson Gymnasium, Joey Lina Gymnasium, Office of Student Affairs and Services (OSAS) Building, Business Affairs Office (BAO), Scholarship and Financial Assistance (SFA) Office, Office of the Registrar, Campus Library, Cashier and Accounting Office, University Health Service / Clinic, Administration Building and Campus Director's Office, Office of the University President, Alumni Building, Gender and Development (GAD) Building, Parking Areas, Comfort Rooms, Transportation to the Campus (Tricycles).

h:additionalInfo: 15 of the 23 programs lead to a PRC licensure examination: BS Psychology (Psychometrician), BS Accountancy (CPA), BS Criminology (Criminologist), BS Fisheries (Fisheries Professional Licensure Examination, formerly the Fisheries Technologist exam), BS Food Technology (Food Technologists Licensure Examination), BS Nutrition and Dietetics (Nutritionist-Dietitian), and all 9 CTE teacher-education programs (Licensure Examination for Teachers: Elementary for BEEd, Secondary for the rest). The 8 programs without a board exam are BS Computer Science, both BS Business Administration majors, the three BS Information Technology majors, BS Tourism Management, and BS Hospitality Management.
h:additionalInfo: All 23 LSPU-LB programs. CAS: BS Psychology. CBAA: BS Accountancy; BS Business Administration major in Marketing Management; BS Business Administration major in Financial Management. CCS: BS Computer Science major in Intelligent Systems; BS Information Technology majors in Animation and Motion Graphics, Web and Mobile Application Development, and Service Management Program. CCJE: BS Criminology. CF: BS Fisheries. CFND: BS Food Technology; BS Nutrition and Dietetics. CIHT: BS Tourism Management; BS Hospitality Management. CTE: BS Education majors in English, Filipino, Mathematics, Sciences, and Social Studies; Bachelor of Elementary Education; Bachelor of Technology and Livelihood Education major in Home Economics; Bachelor of Technical-Vocational Teacher Education major in Food and Service Management; Bachelor of Physical Education.
h:additionalInfo: Campus-wide: the Supreme Student Council (SSC), the main student government. Named organizations: Legion of Lures Esports (LURES), Psychology Society (College of Arts and Sciences), Ka-Peer Yu Organization (peer support, working with the Guidance and Counseling Unit), EsKultura (cultural and arts, with Himig EsKultura and Likha EsKultura), Ritmo EsKultura (official dance club), and Bay Breeze Group of Publications (campus publication). Each of the 8 colleges also has its own student council, including the CCS Student Council (CCS-SC), and the colleges have their own student organizations. Full membership lists were not supplied.
h:additionalInfo: For a life-threatening emergency call 911 (national hotline) and tell the nearest guard. On campus: the Guard House at the main gate (left as you enter) for any security concern; the University Health Service clinic for medical help; the Guidance Office for emotional crisis; and your College Dean for bullying or harassment. The campus main line is (049) 308-4530 (Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM), but it is not an emergency line and it is not answered after office hours; for emergencies use 911 or a guard.
h:additionalInfo: LSPU-LB offers 23 degree programs across 8 colleges. All 23 are 4-year bachelor's programs. By college: College of Teacher Education (CTE) 9; College of Computer Studies (CCS) 4; College of Business Administration and Accountancy (CBAA) 3; College of Food Nutrition and Dietetics (CFND) 2; College of Hospitality Management and Tourism (CIHT) 2; College of Arts and Sciences (CAS) 1; College of Criminal Justice Education (CCJE) 1; College of Fisheries (CF) 1. Of the 23, 15 lead to a PRC licensure examination and 8 do not.
h:additionalInfo: Main events: (1) ICAC-CAF, the sports and cultural competition among colleges; the 2026 campus level was held September 15-18, 2026 and the university-wide ICAC-CAF is scheduled for October 20-23, 2026 at the LSPU Santa Cruz Campus. (2) The LSPU Founding Anniversary; the 73rd was celebrated with activities around November 26-28, 2025. (3) College weeks: each college has its own festival week during the year, such as CCS Week and CTE Week. Also, LURES took part in the 2026 February Fair esports competition.
h:additionalInfo: Office of the Registrar: enrollment, COR, TOR, transfer credentials, grades. Accounting Office: fee assessment and clearance. Cashier: payments. OSAS: student organizations, ID validation, clearances, good moral certificates, excuse slips. Guidance Office: entrance exam and counseling. Scholarship and Financial Assistance Unit: scholarships. University Health Service: medical and dental care. Business Affairs, Marketing and Production Office: Student ID, and the sale of the ID lace, uniform fabric, University shirt, NSTP shirt and PE uniform. ICT office (inside the CCS building): activation of the student portal account. Library: reference, circulation, facilities.
h:additionalInfo: The LSPU-LB campus is in Malinta, Los Baños, Laguna. Directions start at the main gate. Turn left for the Administration Building (Registrar and Cashier/Accounting on the 2nd floor), Joey Lina Gym, CHMT and COF, and CFND beside the Guard House. Walk straight in for the Clinic, Cafeteria, Business Affairs Office and Scholarship and Financial Assistance office. Turn right for the Hall, Gender and Development, CBAA, OSAS, the University President's office, CAS, Lacson Gym, CCS, CTE and the Alumni Building. CCJE is along the road to the right, and the Library is at the end of the road to the left, outside the gate. Places listed: Campus Main Gate and Entrance, Guard House, the Hall, CCS Building (College of Computer Studies), CAS Building (College of Arts and Sciences), CTE Building (College of Teacher Education), CBAA Building (College of Business Administration and Accountancy), CFND Faculty (College of Food Nutrition and Dietetics), CHMT Building (College of Hospitality Management and Tourism), COF Building (College of Fisheries), CCJE Building (College of Criminal Justice Education), Cafeteria, Lacson Gymnasium, Joey Lina Gymnasium, Office of Student Affairs and Services (OSAS) Building, Business Affairs Office (BAO), Scholarship and Financial Assistance (SFA) Office, Office of the Registrar, Campus Library, Cashier and Accounting Office, University Health Service / Clinic, Administration Building and Campus Director's Office, Office of the University President, Alumni Building, Gender and Development (GAD) Building, Parking Areas, Comfort Rooms, Transportation to the Campus (Tricycles).

APPROXIMATE MATCH (not an exhaustive result): Right to Free Higher Education (UniFAST / RA 10687)
h:additionalInfo: Free higher education covers tuition and other school fees for qualified bachelor's degree students.
h:additionalInfo: It does not cover students who do not qualify, students with RLE subjects, opt-out students, CTP/foreign students, and graduate students, who pay through the Accounting Office and Cashier.
h:additionalInfo: Items you buy yourself are separate from tuition: uniform fabric (about Php 600-800, plus tailoring), University shirt (Php 400), NSTP shirt (Php 350), PE T-shirt and shorts (Php 500), ID lace (Php 130), OJT expenses, transport and housing.
h:additionalInfo: Laboratory costs are not on this list: they are already included in the tuition, so a student covered by free higher education pays no separate laboratory fee.
h:additionalInfo: Students not qualified for free higher education, students with RLE subjects, opt-out students, CTP/foreign students, and graduate students go to the Accounting Office for fee assessment and pay at the Cashier.
h:audience: New students

per_item.response:
A COR (Certificate of Registration) is a document certifying that a student is officially enrolled for a semester, required for admission to classes and for processing a student ID. It is issued by the Office of the Registrar and can be viewed online via the student portal or claimed as a printed copy from the Registrar.

A COG (Copy of Grades) is an official record of a student's grades for a semester, issued by the Registrar. It also indicates enrollment status flags such as Warning, Probation, Dismissal, Disqualification, or INC, and is used for retention evaluation and academic standing monitoring.

The main difference is that the COR certifies enrollment status for a semester, while the COG provides academic performance and status information for that semester.
per_item.reference: The COR (Certificate of Registration) certifies that you are officially enrolled for the semester; it is required for admission to classes and for processing a student ID, and can be viewed on the portal or claimed as a printed copy at the Registrar. The COG (Copy of Grades) is the official record of your grades for a semester issued by the Registrar; its information is also shown on the LSPU Portal.

SECTION: Chapter 6 CODE OF CONDUCT FOR LSPU STUDENTS (Definition and Type of Offenses) | Article 3. Minor Offense
Article 3. Minor Offense

Sec. 1. Attendance

1.1. Attending flag raising and flag lowering ceremonies (R.A. 8491 Sec. 18 and 50 Philippine Flag Law), classes, and other required University activities regularly and on time is required for all students unless exemption is granted by the University President or his duly authorized representative.

1.2 Tardiness and absences shall be dealt with as follows:

1.2.1 Tardiness in all activities where student’s attendance is required shall be considered one (1) absence in class.

1.2.2 Three (3) tardiness in a class shall be considered one (1) absence from the same.
 1st Offense: One (1) day absent plus community service
 2nd Offense: Inform the parents/guardians with three (3) days suspension
 3rd Offense: Suspension for one (1) week

1.2.3. Every student accumulating unexcused absences from class equivalent to 17% of the total number of hours/ semester for a particular subject or class shall be dropped from the roll of students. However, excused absences can be removed through makeup.

1.2.4. Every student shall secure an excuse slip from the Guidance Office for absence/s made before admission to classes.

Sec. 2. Dishonesty.

SOURCE: LSPU_SOURCE.txt | CHUNK: pillar3_txt_chunk_448
SECTION: Chapter 3 | Article 8. Attendance
Article 8. Attendance

Sec. 1. Policy. A student absent from classes for unavoidable cause must obtain an excuse slip from the Office of the Students Affairs Services or Guidance Office. The slip must be presented to the instructor/ professor concerned not later than the second class session, following the student’s return with a medical certification for absence due to illness.

Sec. 2. Absence. A student accumulating unexcused absences from class, equivalent to twenty percent (25%) of the total number of hours per day session for a particular subject, shall be dropped from the roll of students for the particular subject or class, as the case may be. Time lost due to late enrolment shall be considered as a time lost by absence.
per_item.response: Three (3) tardiness instances count as one (1) absence.
per_item.reference: Three (3) tardiness instances in a class count as one (1) absence (Student Handbook, Ch. 6 Art. 3 Sec. 1).

per_item.response:
The steps to request a Transcript of Records are as follows:

1. Fill out and endorse request slip:
   - Agency Action: Issues request slip (LSPU-REG-SF-011); reviews and checks the accomplished request against the student's clearance; assesses the corresponding fees of the requested documents.
   - Client Action: Undergraduate students fill out the request slip with clearance and secure signatures of heads of responsible offices; graduates fill out the same request slip.
   - Processing Time: 5 minutes
   - Next Step: Pay required fees

2. Pay required fees:
   - Agency Action: Receives payment and issues official receipt.
   - Client Action: Proceeds to the Cashier's Office to pay the required fees.
   - Fees: P75.00/page (undergraduate), P150.00/page (graduate), among others
   - Processing Time: 2 minutes
   - Next Step: Submit receipt and request slip; receive claim stub; document preparation

3. Submit receipt and request slip; receive claim stub; document preparation:
   - Agency Action: Receives and reviews the presented receipt and request slip; schedules the date of release; issues claim stub; locates the permanent record of the student concerned; prepares and encodes the requested document; reviews and counterchecks entries on the draft; prints the final document; affixes the college seal; signs the document.
   - Client Action: Submits the filled-out request slip and official receipt; gets the claim stub with date of release.
   - Processing Time: Up to 59 minutes total (including locating record, preparing, reviewing, printing, sealing, and signing)
   - Next Step: Claim requested document

4. Claim requested document:
   - Agency Action: Records and releases the document.
   - Client Action: Claims the requested document on the scheduled date indicated on the claim stub.
   - Processing Time: 2 minutes
per_item.reference: Step 1: fill out the request slip (LSPU-REG-SF-011) with clearance and signatures of the heads of responsible offices; graduates fill out the same slip. Step 2: pay the required fees at the Cashier's Office (TOR is P75.00 per page for undergraduate and P150.00 per page for graduate). Step 3: submit the request slip and official receipt and receive a claim stub with the release date while the Registrar prepares the document. Step 4: claim the document on the date on the claim stub. Total service time is up to 59 minutes for active files and 1 day plus about 44 minutes for inactive files.

Source: LSPU official website admission pages, text supplied by the maintainer (September 2026); not from the Handbook or Citizen's Charter (Transfer within LSPU / Shifting of Course). Compare with the Handbook shifting and transferring rules above.
A student who has earned at least 30 collegiate academic units and wants to move from one course to another files an application for transfer or shifting in the current college. It is referred to the accepting college together with a true copy of grades. If the accepting college approves, the student receives a permit to transfer and a copy of grades.
Shifting is not allowed without a valid reason. The student must qualify for the grade requirements of the department being entered. The application uses the prescribed form stating the reasons, with a copy of grades certified by the registrar. The College Dean must approve it, and it goes to the VPAA/Campus Director for approval, before 12% of the regular class meetings of the term have been held. A request submitted or received later is not considered for the following semester.

Source: LSPU official website admission pages, text supplied by the maintainer (September 2026); not from the Handbook or Citizen's Charter (Transfer Admission: Transfer within LSPU System).
Students from another LSPU constituent campus who have earned at least 30 collegiate academic units may be admitted as transferees, subject to the rules of the admitting college. The student must present honorable dismissal from the college or university last attended; must complete in LSPU at least 50% of the units required for the program (75% if running for honors); and the University's quota must not yet be filled.
An admitted transferee may not enroll in a subject whose prerequisite, taken elsewhere, has not been validated or repeated in LSPU. All courses for which advanced credit is sought must be validated at the time stated in the validation requirements.

To apply online for the completion of an INC grade at LSPU-LB campus, follow these steps:

1. Submit the complete requirements to the subject teacher.
2. Log in to the LSPU online system portal (myaccount.lspu.edu.ph).
3. Apply online for the completion of the INC or 4.0 grade through the portal (this step takes approximately 5 minutes).
4. Pay the corresponding completion fee of P30.00 per unit at the cashier’s office (processing time is about 5 minutes).
5. The cashier will put the official receipt number on the completion form in the online system.
6. Inform the subject teacher that you have applied online for the completion of your INC grade.
7. The subject teacher will give the corresponding grades through the online system.
8. The college dean or associate dean will check and approve the request.
9. The registrar will verify if the INC or 4.0 grade has been changed.

Required documents:
- Completion form
- Proof of payment (official cashier receipt)

Total processing time is 25 minutes.

SECTION: Chapter 3 | Article 8. Attendance
Article 8. Attendance

Sec. 1. Policy. A student absent from classes for unavoidable cause must obtain an excuse slip from the Office of the Students Affairs Services or Guidance Office. The slip must be presented to the instructor/ professor concerned not later than the second class session, following the student’s return with a medical certification for absence due to illness.

Sec. 2. Absence. A student accumulating unexcused absences from class, equivalent to twenty percent (25%) of the total number of hours per day session for a particular subject, shall be dropped from the roll of students for the particular subject or class, as the case may be. Time lost due to late enrolment shall be considered as a time lost by absence.

Article 3. Minor Offense

Sec. 1. Attendance

1.1. Attending flag raising and flag lowering ceremonies (R.A. 8491 Sec. 18 and 50 Philippine Flag Law), classes, and other required University activities regularly and on time is required for all students unless exemption is granted by the University President or his duly authorized representative.

1.2 Tardiness and absences shall be dealt with as follows:

1.2.1 Tardiness in all activities where student’s attendance is required shall be considered one (1) absence in class.

1.2.2 Three (3) tardiness in a class shall be considered one (1) absence from the same.
 1st Offense: One (1) day absent plus community service
 2nd Offense: Inform the parents/guardians with three (3) days suspension
 3rd Offense: Suspension for one (1) week

1.2.3. Every student accumulating unexcused absences from class equivalent to 17% of the total number of hours/ semester for a particular subject or class shall be dropped from the roll of students. However, excused absences can be removed through makeup.

1.2.4. Every student shall secure an excuse slip from the Guidance Office for absence/s made before admission to classes.

Sec. 2. Dishonesty.

A student accumulating absences from class which is equivalent to twenty percent (20%) of the total number of hour per day session for a particular subject shall be dropped from the roll of students for the particular subject or class. Time lost due to late enrolment shall be considered as a time lost by absence.

Sec. 2. Sports, other non-academic activities, and academic commitments at other institutions will not normally be accepted as valid reasons for approving absences from any arranged course activities in the university.

Source: general description of each Google tool and how the campus mainly uses it (maintainer and project team, September 2026).
- Google Classroom (online class management): join a class with a class code, read posted lessons and announcements, receive assignments, and submit outputs online.
- Google Meet (online meetings and classes): attend online lectures, consultations, and group meetings by video call.
- Gmail (school email): receive announcements from teachers, offices, and the college, and send school-related messages using the school Google account.
- Google Calendar (schedules and reminders): keep track of class schedules, deadlines, and school events, and receive reminders.
- Google Drive, Docs, Sheets and Slides (file storage and collaborative documents): store files in the cloud and write reports, spreadsheets, and presentations, alone or with groupmates, with shared editing.

Article 7. Composition, Administration, Coverage and Jurisdiction of the Student Discipline Committee

Sec. 1. Definition. Student discipline refers to the desired and/or expected norm of conduct of students, and the corresponding administrative sanctions thereof, as set forth in this duly approved and promulgated Code of Conduct of LSPU Students and /or College Rules and Regulations.

Sec. 2. Composition of Student Discipline Committee. The Student Discipline Committee shall be composed of the following:

2.1. Chairman /Chairperson: Director/Chairperson for Student Affairs and Services

2.2. Vice Chairman/Vice Chairperson: Student Discipline Coordinator

2.3. Members: Vice President for Academic Affairs/Campus Director, Dean of College where the student is enrolled, Chief Security Officer ,President of Supreme Student Council

2.4. University Legal Consultant

Sec. 3. Administration. The Office of the Student Affairs and Services

(OSAS) shall handle all complaints against alleged violators of the Code of Conduct of LSPU Students and/or College Rules and Regulations.

Cases must be treated individually according to their merits and findings of investigations.

Yes. All 8 colleges (CAS, CBAA, CCS, CCJE, CF, CFND, CIHT and CTE) have their own student council, and there is one Supreme Student Council (SSC) that governs them at the campus level.
The Supreme Student Council is the student body duly managed and elected at large by the students themselves; its President sits on the Student Discipline Committee and its Federated President sits on the Board. At LSPU-LB it is the main campus-wide student government: it represents students and helps organize campus-wide activities, programs, and student initiatives.

Sec. 1. Academic Load The student's academic load shall consist of a combination of units of credit, the total of which shall be determined by the student’s curricular program.

1.3. Overload. No student is allowed to take more than the normal load during the term/semester. per_item.user_input: Who can I contact in an emergency on campus?
retrieved_contexts:
SOURCE: LSPU_SOURCE.txt | CHUNK: pillar3_txt_chunk_779
SECTION: WHO TO CONTACT IN AN EMERGENCY ON CAMPUS (SUMMARY)
WHO TO CONTACT IN AN EMERGENCY ON CAMPUS (SUMMARY)
Source: compiled from campus information supplied by the maintainer; 911 is general national information.
For a life-threatening emergency, call 911 (the national emergency hotline) and tell the nearest guard.
On campus:
- The Guard House at the main gate (on the left as you enter) for any security concern.
- The University Health Service clinic for medical help.
- The Guidance Office for an emotional or mental health crisis.
- Your College Dean for bullying or harassment.
The campus main line is (049) 308-4530 (Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM), but it is not an emergency line and it is not answered after office hours. For emergencies use 911 or a guard.
Only the campus main line is documented. Direct numbers for the guards, clinic and Guidance Office have not been supplied.

SECTION: EMERGENCY CONTACT: CAMPUS GUARDS AND THE GUARD HOUSE (SAFETY AND SECURITY)
EMERGENCY CONTACT: CAMPUS GUARDS AND THE GUARD HOUSE (SAFETY AND SECURITY)
Source: campus map (location); Student Handbook (role of the Safety and Security Management Office); no phone number available.
For an emergency on campus, tell the nearest guard or go to the Guard House at the main gate (on the left as you enter). The Safety and Security Management Office handles security concerns.
Go to the guards for: fights, threats, suspicious persons, fire, accidents, and lost and found items.
No direct security phone number has been documented. The campus main line (049) 308-4530 (Mon-Fri, 8:00 AM-5:00 PM) is general, not an emergency line. For emergencies use 911 or go to the Guard House.

Source: general national information (not an LSPU document).
911 is the Philippine national emergency hotline. Call it for police, fire, ambulance and other urgent emergencies anywhere in the Philippines, including on or near the campus. Call it for a crime in progress, fire, serious injury or any life-threatening situation, then inform the campus guard as soon as you can.

SOURCE: LSPU_SOURCE.txt | CHUNK: pillar3_txt_chunk_782

Source: Citizen's Charter 2026, University Health Service, Service 1, p. 14; the 911 advice is general safety information.
The University Health Service (campus clinic) gives routine medical and dental consultation at no fee. Go there when you feel sick, have minor injuries, or need a first medical assessment on campus.
For a serious injury or life-threatening condition, call 911 and tell a guard rather than waiting for a clinic visit.
No direct clinic phone number has been supplied. The campus main line is (049) 308-4530 (Mon-Fri, 8:00 AM-5:00 PM); confirm the clinic's own hours.

Source: Student Handbook Chapter 5, Article 1, Sec. 2 and the Mental Health Services articles; the 911 advice and the office location are from the maintainer and general safety information.
The Guidance Office (inside the OSAS building) offers counseling and mental health support to enrolled students. Go there for emotional distress, mental health concerns, and support after a bullying or harassment incident.
If you or someone else is in immediate danger, call 911 first.
No direct Guidance Office phone number has been supplied. The campus main line is (049) 308-4530 (Mon-Fri, 8:00 AM-5:00 PM).

The university offers the following mental health services:

1. Assessment, counseling, and referral for students with mental health concerns, including minors aged 15-17 with consent and assent.
2. Guidance and counseling services, including individual and group counseling, case conferences with parents/students, and follow-up/referral to a multidisciplinary team.
3. Clinic-based evaluations conducted by psychologists, counselors, and nurses.
4. Outreach services for adolescents with complex mental health needs, including mobile youth outreach services.
5. Early intervention programs in schools to reduce conduct disorder prevalence and impact.
6. Psychological and educational assistance through a peer facilitators program.
7. Consultation and referrals to community support services, including school support for students and their families.
per_item.reference: The university offers Mental Health Counseling and Referral (assessment, counseling, and referral for enrolled students; university health service personnel may assess students aged 15-17 with consent and assent) and Guidance and Counseling Services (individual and group counseling, case conferences with parents or students, and follow-up or referral to a multidisciplinary team). The Guidance Office, inside the OSAS building, offers counseling and mental health support.

CCJE: BS Criminology. CF: BS Fisheries. CFND: BS Food Technology; BS Nutrition and Dietetics. CIHT: BS Tourism Management; BS Hospitality Management. h:additionalInfo: Campus-wide: the Supreme Student Council (SSC), the main student government. Named organizations: Legion of Lures Esports (LURES), Psychology Society (College of Arts and Sciences), Ka-Peer Yu Organization (peer support, working with the Guidance and Counseling Unit), EsKultura (cultural and arts, with Himig EsKultura and Likha EsKultura), Ritmo EsKultura (official dance club), and Bay Breeze Group of Publications (campus publication). Each of the 8 colleges also has its own student council, including the CCS Student Council (CCS-SC), and the colleges have their own student organizations. Full membership lists were not supplied.
h:additionalInfo: For a life-threatening emergency call 911 (national hotline) and tell the nearest guard. On campus: the Guard House at the main gate (left as you enter) for any security concern; the University Health Service clinic for medical help; the Guidance Office for emotional crisis; and your College Dean for bullying or harassment. The campus main line is (049) 308-4530 (Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM), but it is not an emergency line and it is not answered after office hours; for emergencies use 911 or a guard.
h:additionalInfo: LSPU-LB offers 23 degree programs across 8 colleges. All 23 are 4-year bachelor's programs. By college: College of Teacher Education (CTE) 9; College of Computer Studies (CCS) 4; College of Business Administration and Accountancy (CBAA) 3; College of Food Nutrition and Dietetics (CFND) 2; College of Hospitality Management and Tourism (CIHT) 2; College of Arts and Sciences (CAS) 1; College of Criminal Justice Education (CCJE) 1; College of Fisheries (CF) 1. Of the 23, 15 lead to a PRC licensure examination and 8 do not.
h:additionalInfo: Main events: (1) ICAC-CAF, the sports and cultural competition among colleges; the 2026 campus level was held September 15-18, 2026 and the university-wide ICAC-CAF is scheduled for October 20-23, 2026 at the LSPU Santa Cruz Campus. (2) The LSPU Founding Anniversary; the 73rd was celebrated with activities around November 26-28, 2025. (3) College weeks: each college has its own festival week during the year, such as CCS Week and CTE Week. Also, LURES took part in the 2026 February Fair esports competition.
h:additionalInfo: Office of the Registrar: enrollment, COR, TOR, transfer credentials, grades. Accounting Office: fee assessment and clearance. Cashier: payments. OSAS: student organizations, ID validation, clearances, good moral certificates, excuse slips. Guidance Office: entrance exam and counseling. Scholarship and Financial Assistance Unit: scholarships. University Health Service: medical and dental care. Business Affairs, Marketing and Production Office: Student ID, and the sale of the ID lace, uniform fabric, University shirt, NSTP shirt and PE uniform. ICT office (inside the CCS building): activation of the student portal account. Library: reference, circulation, facilities.
h:additionalInfo: The LSPU-LB campus is in Malinta, Los Baños, Laguna. Directions start at the main gate. Turn left for the Administration Building (Registrar and Cashier/Accounting on the 2nd floor), Joey Lina Gym, CHMT and COF, and CFND beside the Guard House. Source: checked by the maintainer against RA 11398, RA 11052 and PRC announcements (general public information, not an LSPU document). The Pillar 1 program blocks above use "Fisheries Professional Licensure Examination" and "Food Technologist Licensure Examination".
BS Fisheries: the official current name is the Fisheries Professional Licensure Examination, under RA 11398 (Philippine Fisheries Profession Act, 2019), which speaks of the licensure examination for fisheries professionals. The earlier law (RA 8550 / PRC Res. 2000-664) called the practitioners fisheries technologists, and PRC web pages still list the board type as Fisheries Technologists. Other names for the same exam: Fisheries Technologist Licensure Examination, Fisheries Technologists Licensure Examination, Fisheries Professionals Licensure Examination, and "Fisheries board exam".
BS Food Technology: under RA 11052 (Philippine Food Technology Act), PRC uses the plural "Food Technologists Licensure Examination", and 2026 PRC announcements call it the "Professional Food Technologists Computer-Based Licensure Examination".

LSPU-LB ACADEMIC PROGRAMS: OVERVIEW
Laguna State Polytechnic University - Los Banos Campus (LSPU-LB) offers 23 degree programs across 8 colleges. All programs are four-year programs.

Colleges and the programs they offer:
- College of Arts and Sciences (CAS): Bachelor of Science in Psychology
- College of Business Administration and Accountancy (CBAA): Bachelor of Science in Business Administration - Major in Marketing Management; Bachelor of Science in Accountancy; Bachelor of Science in Business Administration - Major in Financial Management
- College of Computer Studies (CCS): Bachelor of Science in Computer Science - Major in Intelligent Systems; Bachelor of Science in Information Technology - Major in Animation and Motion Graphics; Bachelor of Science in Information Technology - Major in Web and Mobile Application Development; Bachelor of Science in Information Technology - Major in Service Management Program
- College of Criminal Justice Education (CCJE): Bachelor of Science in Criminology
- College of Fisheries (CF): Bachelor of Science in Fisheries

SOURCE: LSPU_SOURCE.txt | CHUNK: pillar3_txt_chunk_789
SECTION: STUDENT ORGANIZATIONS AT LSPU-LB (OVERVIEW)
STUDENT ORGANIZATIONS AT LSPU-LB (OVERVIEW)
Source: campus information supplied by the maintainer (September 2026); not from the Handbook or Citizen's Charter.
Campus-wide: the Supreme Student Council (SSC), the main student government.
Named organizations: Legion of Lures Esports (LURES), Psychology Society (College of Arts and Sciences), Ka-Peer Yu Organization (peer support, working with the Guidance and Counseling Unit), EsKultura (cultural and arts, with Himig EsKultura and Likha EsKultura), Ritmo EsKultura (official dance club), and Bay Breeze Group of Publications (campus publication).
Each of the 8 colleges also has its own student council, including the CCS Student Council (CCS-SC), and the colleges have their own student organizations. Full membership lists were not supplied.

SOURCE: LSPU_SOURCE.txt | CHUNK: pillar3_txt_chunk_797
SECTION: STUDENT COUNCILS AT LSPU-LB: SUPREME STUDENT COUNCIL AND THE EIGHT COLLEGE COUNCILS
STUDENT COUNCILS AT LSPU-LB: SUPREME STUDENT COUNCIL AND THE EIGHT COLLEGE COUNCILS
Source: Student Handbook Chapter 5, Article 2, Sec. 3 (SSC definition); campus information supplied by the maintainer (September 2026).
Yes. All 8 colleges (CAS, CBAA, CCS, CCJE, CF, CFND, CIHT and CTE) have their own student council, and there is one Supreme Student Council (SSC) that governs them at the campus level.
The Supreme Student Council is the student body duly managed and elected at large by the students themselves; its President sits on the Student Discipline Committee and its Federated President sits on the Board. At LSPU-LB it is the main campus-wide student government: it represents students and helps organize campus-wide activities, programs, and student initiatives.

CAMPUS EVENTS AT LSPU-LB (SUMMARY)
Source: campus information supplied by the maintainer (September 2026). Event dates were supplied by the maintainer, are time-sensitive, and were not independently confirmed (status as of September 29, 2026).
Main events:
(1) ICAC-CAF, the sports and cultural competition among colleges. The 2026 campus level was held September 15-18, 2026, and the university-wide ICAC-CAF is scheduled for October 20-23, 2026 at the LSPU Santa Cruz Campus.
(2) The LSPU Founding Anniversary. The 73rd was celebrated with activities around November 26-28, 2025.
(3) College weeks: each college has its own festival week during the year, such as CCS Week and CTE Week.
Also, LURES took part in the 2026 February Fair esports competition.

Sec. 5. INC Mark

5.1. Types of INC or Incomplete mark

5.1.1. No Final Examination. A grade of INC is given if a student whose class standing throughout the term/semester is passing but fails to take the final examination due to illness or other valid reason/s. An approved excuse slip is required before a student is given the examination. In case the student's class standing is not passing, and s/he fails the final examination for any reason, a grade of “5.0” is given. Re-examination to improve a passing grade is not allowed.

5.1.2. Failure to comply with certain requirements. INC is also given to the work that is of passing quality, but some parts of which are undone because of sickness or failure to comply with certain requirements of the course.

5.2. Policies for INC

5.2.1. A grade of INC is not given to any student with a failing grade in a subject. The one-year academic period is interrupted as extending to the regular semester; the removal period immediately follows the one year.

Article 2. Definition of Terms

1.1. Industry refers to companies involved in services and production of goods for sale especially in a factory.

1.2. Internship refers to a period of time spent receiving or completing training at a job both to apply classroom learning and to be exposed to professional workplace.

1.3. Host Training Establishment (HTE) refers to agencies, institutions, or establishments whom the University has partnered with and entrusted the students for work immersion and learning experience.

1.4. Internship Manual refers to the document detailing the policies and guidelines for the conduct of the internship/on-the-job training of the students.

1.5. Internship Plan refers to the curriculum and competency outline detailing what the student should be able to attain in the course of the internship/on-the-job training program as prepared and approved by the University and the HTE.

1.6. Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) refers to the document that records the details of an agreement between the University and the HTE, detailing the objectives, plan, scope, expectations and activities among other composites of the agreement.

per_item.response:
The difference between a COR (Certificate of Registration) and a COG (Copy of Grades) is as follows:

- A COR (Certificate of Registration) is a document certifying that a student is officially enrolled for a semester. It is required for admission to classes and can be viewed online via the student portal or claimed as a printed copy from the Registrar's Office. The process to view it online takes about 3 minutes, while claiming a printed copy takes about 20 minutes.

- A COG (Copy of Grades) is an official record of a student's grades for a semester issued by the Registrar at the end of each semester. It also indicates enrollment status flags such as Warning, Probation, Dismissal, Disqualification, or INC. It is used by the College Dean for retention evaluation and by students to monitor their academic standing.

In summary:
1. COR certifies enrollment status; COG details academic performance and standing.
2. COR is issued upon enrollment; COG is issued at the end of the semester.
3. Viewing COR online takes about 3 minutes; claiming a printed COR takes about 20 minutes.
4. COG includes grades and enrollment flags, used for academic evaluation.
per_item.reference: The COR (Certificate of Registration) certifies that you are officially enrolled for the semester; it is required for admission to classes and for processing a student ID, and can be viewed on the portal or claimed as a printed copy at the Registrar. The COG (Copy of Grades) is the official record of your grades for a semester issued by the Registrar; its information is also shown on the LSPU Portal.

The GWA cutoff is strict. If your GWA is below the minimum for the program you want, you cannot be admitted to it; your only option is to choose another program with a lower cutoff.
Example: a GWA of 86 qualifies only for the GWA-85 programs.
Cutoffs for 1st Sem AY 2026-2027: GWA 85 for the three BS Information Technology majors, BS Criminology and BS Hospitality Management (5 programs); GWA 87 for BS Fisheries, BTLE and BTVTE (3); GWA 88 for BS Psychology, both BS Business Administration majors and BS Tourism Management (4); GWA 90 for Accountancy, Computer Science, Food Technology, Nutrition and Dietetics, Physical Education, all five BS Education majors and Elementary Education (11).
Meeting the cutoff is not enough by itself: applicants must still pass the entrance exam and interview.

SECTION: Chapter 3 | Article 7. Grading System and Other Grade-related Concerns
of GWA

4.1. GWA. The General Weighted Average or GWA of students refers to the weighted average of grades in all academic courses taken in a given semester.

4.2. Cumulative GWA. Cumulative GWA is the weighted average of the grades in all academic courses from the first semester in which the student was enrolled up to the second semester just finished.

Sec. 5. Policy on Grades of “4” and “5”

5.1. Appearance of “4”. To compute the General Weighted Average

(GWA) of a student with a grade of “4”, use the latter as an actual grade on the premise that “4” is conditional.

5.2. Appearance of “5”. If the student gets a removal grade of “5”, this grade is included in the computation of the GWA together with the grade which s/he gets after re-enrolling and passing the course.

The GWA should be the basis for determining if the student graduates with or without honors.

5.3. Removal Policy for “4.00”. A grade of “4.00” may be removed by repeating the subject or by re-examination. The highest grade a student must obtain upon re-examination is “3.00”. If the removal examination is failed, a student is given a grade of “5.00”.
